assignments.reason: Although this compound concept spans both Torah and prayer, its essential function in Torah #8 is as the combined practice through which one clarifies halakha and separates good from evil. The Torah text (§6) frames it as the practical prescription: 'להפריש ולהבדיל ולבטל הרע מהטוב הוא על ידי תורה ותפלה'. Since Torah is the actualization (בריאה בפועל) and prayer feeds wisdom into Torah, and the emphasis is on the practical application (learning poskim), the combined concept belongs in the Torah/Actual Creation package — it IS Torah-practice augmented by prayer.

Separating good from evil is the essential activity of Torah study in this teaching. The text (§6) explains that Torah contains the mixture of permitted/forbidden, pure/impure, and the act of clarifying halakha IS the separation of good from evil. This concept's essential nature is the operative function of Torah — the actual creation/actualization process of distinguishing right from wrong through legal study.

Receiving the Torah is essentially a Torah-domain concept. The proof text (edge 2266) explicitly frames it via 'רכב אלקים רבותים' = receiving the Torah at Sinai, from which the holy rabbis receive ruach-chaim. Its essential nature is the foundational act of Torah — the moment Torah entered the world as actual creation.

The fulfillment of one's request is essentially the actualization of prayer. The proof text (edge 2122) explains: 'בהתפלה עדיין הוא בכח ואינו יוצא אל הפועל, עד שבא אל התורה... ואזי נעשה בקשתו'. The request (בקשה) is born in prayer; its fulfillment is the telos of the prayer process. Its essential nature is the completion of the prayer cycle — the moment potential (prayer) becomes actual.

assignments.node_id: כשהוא מקשר להצדיק והרב שבדור, כשהוא מתאנח ומאריך רוחה
assignments.reason: This concept describes the practice of connecting to the tzaddik and sighing — extending one's breath. Its essential nature is the mechanism of drawing ruach-chaim. The Torah text (§2) explains: 'וכשהוא מקשר להצדיק... כשהוא מתאנח ומאריך רוחה, ממשיך רוח החיים'. The sighing and breath-extension IS the drawing of the spirit; its nature belongs to the ruach-chaim domain.

Drawing the ruach-chaim from the tzaddik is essentially about the flow of the spirit of life. The node's very name contains 'רוח החיים' — its essential nature is the transmission of the holy life-breath. It is the process by which ruach-chaim reaches people, which belongs squarely in the Breath of Life package.

Sighing over the deficiency and extending breath — this is fundamentally a ruach/breathing concept. The Torah text (§1) identifies the sigh (אנחה) as the extension of breath (אריכת הנשימה), which is the very mechanism of drawing ruach-chaim. Its essential nature is breath-extension, the same domain as אנחה and ארך אפים already in Package 1.

assignments.node_id: רוח החיים, שלמות החסרון, שממשיכין מהצדיק על־ידי אנחה
assignments.reason: This compound node explicitly names 'רוח החיים' and 'שלמות החסרון' — the ruach-chaim and the completion of deficiency drawn from the tzaddik through sighing. Every element of this concept (ruach, completion, tzaddik, sighing) belongs to the Breath of Life domain. The node essentially summarizes the entire Package 1 mechanism.

Completing the deficiency is essentially what the ruach-chaim accomplishes. The Torah text (§1) says: 'על ידי האנחה משלים החסרון' — through the sigh, the deficiency is completed. Package 1 already contains שלמות החסרון, נתמלא החסרון, and מלאפום — all expressing the same essential nature of the ruach filling what is lacking. This node shares that essential nature.

Subduing and toppling all enemies is the result of the tzaddik's drawing of ruach-chaim. The proof text cites Zechariah 4:6 'לא בחיל ולא בכח כי אם ברוחי' — 'not by might nor by power but by My spirit.' The concept's essential nature is the power of the holy spirit to overcome opposition. It is a manifestation of ruach-chaim's potency, belonging to the spirit-of-life domain.

Subduing the storm-wind is the direct victory of the holy ruach-chaim over the impure ruach. The proof text (edge 1806) explains that through the four tzitzit (= ruach-chaim from four winds), the ruach-se'ara of the opponents is subdued. The concept is essentially about the triumph of the holy wind; its nature is the power dimension of ruach-chaim.

Subduing him (Esav/evil) through the holy tallit. The proof text (edge 1805) explains: 'על ידי טלית דקדושה... מכניעין אותו כי משם נמשך הרוח חיים דקדושה'. The tallit is already in Package 1 as an expression of ruach-chaim. The subduing is the manifestation of that same holy spirit's power over evil.

The tzaddikim prevailing over the wicked is explicitly attributed to the ruach-chaim: 'כי על ידי הרוח חיים הנ"ל מתגברין הצדיקים על הרשעים'. This is the collective victory dimension of ruach-chaim — the spirit of life empowering the righteous. Its essential nature is the power of holy breath.

The spirit of klipa being subdued — this node's essential nature IS the impure spirit (רוח דקלפה). It describes the state of the evil wind being defeated. The concept named is the evil wind itself (in a state of subjugation). Its nature belongs to the evil-domain package of Esav and the impure wind, as it is that very impure wind being referenced.

The tallit of klipa being subdued — this node's essential nature IS the evil tallit (טלית דקלפה), which is already identified in Package 4 as Esav's red garment. The concept being named is the evil garment itself (in a state of defeat). It belongs to the Esav/impure-wind domain.

assignments.node_id: נתבטלין ונכנעין אלופי עשו, רברבי עשו
assignments.reason: The nullification and subjugation of the chiefs of Esav (אלופי עשו, רברבי עשו). The concepts named — אלופי עשו and רברבי עשו — are already in Package 4. This node describes those same evil commanders being defeated. Its essential nature is the Esav domain: these are Esav's officers, the רב דקלפה's army.

Atonement of sins through the ruach-chaim. The Torah text (§4) explains: 'הצדיק הממשיך רוח החיים ומשלים החסרון מכפר העון' and 'ואיש חכם יכפרנה'. The proof text (edge 2275) ties atonement directly to ruach-chaim drawn from the tzaddik through sighing. Atonement here is essentially a function of the life-spirit's completion of deficiency — it is what happens when ruach-chaim fills the void caused by sin. Its nature is the healing/restorative dimension of the Breath of Life.
